pressR

pressR parses, analyzes, and visualizes pressure distribution data from capacitive sensor systems. It ships with predefined layouts for in-shoe pressure measurement, saddle pressure mapping (equine and bicycle), seating assessment, and barefoot pedography, along with an interactive Shiny application for data exploration.

Successor release status

Version 0.3.0 (developed as 0.2.0.9000) corrects audited import, unit and reproducibility problems. The manuscript baseline remains at commit 5f5b370 (0.1.0). Do not replace a manuscript environment silently: retain its version and saved cycle references, and review the migration notes in NEWS.md.

To reproduce an analysis that used the frozen manuscript baseline, install that exact source in a separate R library:

baseline_lib <- path.expand("~/R/pressR-manuscript-0.1.0")
dir.create(baseline_lib, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
pak::pak("CTTIR/pressR@5f5b370890fafae01b78174a1cec52b4a2039ce3",
         lib = baseline_lib)
# In a fresh R session for that manuscript:
.libPaths(c(baseline_lib, .libPaths()))

The successor is experimental software; local software checks do not establish clinical or study-specific validity.

Installation

Use R 4.1 or newer. Install the development source and its required dependencies:

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("CTTIR/pressR")

HTML reports additionally need rmarkdown and Pandoc (included with RStudio). PDF reports also need a LaTeX installation, such as TinyTeX. Workbook and archive imports respectively need the optional readxl and archive packages.

install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "tinytex"))  # For HTML and PDF reports
tinytex::install_tinytex()                  # If LaTeX is not already installed

Quick example 

library(pressR)

trial <- pr_example_trial("insole")

pr_plot_heatmap(trial)
pr_plot_force_time(trial, show_cycles = TRUE)

pr_summary(trial)
pr_calc_regional(trial)
pr_run_app(trial)  # Opens the interactive explorer

Features

  • Parsers for ASCII pressure data exports, generic CSV, force sensor data, and region mask files (.msa/.msr/.msp).
  • Predefined layouts for in-shoe insoles (99-sensor), barefoot pressure platforms, generic sensor mats (16x16 / 32x32), horse and bicycle saddles, wheelchair / car / office seating, and glove sensors.
  • Per-frame and per-trial analysis: peak pressure, mean pressure, force, contact area, pressure-time integral, center of pressure, symmetry index, gait cycle detection, and COP rollover pattern.
  • Application-specific analysis: saddle bridge and slip detection, wheelchair hotspot identification, plantar-pressure regional analysis.
  • Traceable reference observations with source, study context and status. Nyikos (2005) is the source of the six saddle observations; unsupported legacy thresholds are withdrawn. Overlays require explicit compatible context.
  • Study assets: lossless workbook cell retention with normalized HR/RR series, image metadata registration, bounded archive extraction and explicit-key links.
  • Interchange: version 2 trial bundles preserve exact measurements and timing, layout, units, factor levels and metadata with SHA-256 integrity checks.
  • Visualization: 2D and 3D heatmaps, dynamics plots, regional bar charts, composite report panels, and side-by-side trial comparison.
  • Shiny app (pr_run_app()) for interactive import, analysis, and export.

Real recordings and reproducibility 

trial <- pr_read_auto("recording.asc")
pr_summary_long(trial)  # Values, units, and availability
pr_write_bundle(trial, "recording-bundle")
restored <- pr_read_bundle("recording-bundle")
analysis <- pr_temporal_profile(trial, "corrected")

New bundles store authoritative measurements in measurements.rds and provide pressure.csv as a nonbinding preview for inspection and exchange. Reading checks the preview’s checksum and structure; analyses use the RDS values. Recreate the bundle to change measurements. This avoids decimal round-trip changes that can invalidate measurement-bound cycle references. Version 1 bundles remain readable, with their original decimal precision limits. Only read bundles from trusted sources: they contain serialized R objects, and checksums detect corruption without authenticating the sender.

CSV and report exports refuse recorded source paths and symbolic-link targets. They finish writing before replacing an existing output and restore it after a reported replacement failure, or report the retained backup path if restoration fails. These guarantees do not cover process termination or simultaneous writers.

Pliance detection uses the file header, including temporary upload paths. CSV round trips recognize exported timestamps and sensor identifiers. Incomplete or malformed generic inputs are rejected instead of padded, truncated or zero-filled. Pliance missing-frame handling is explicit and recorded in metadata.

Numeric text imports accept nonzero magnitudes from 1e-290 through 1e290 and check for gross conversion errors. These checks add parsing time: one synthetic 10,000-frame, 256-sensor CSV took 6.59 seconds versus 0.72 seconds in the preserved baseline on the audit machine, with identical imported values. This single fixture is not a general performance guarantee. Version 2 bundles preserve finite binary measurements beyond that text-import range.

Unknown sensor area or pitch stays unknown. Novel saddle recordings display in grid units; physical force and contact area remain unavailable until calibrated. Force-sensor inputs already measured in newtons are summed directly. Negative sensor offsets are retained and counted for review.

pr_temporal_profile() offers corrected, legacy_method, and reference. Corrected analysis uses measured timing and deterministic plateau handling. Legacy method retains the historical 50 Hz assumptions but is not an exact replay guarantee. Use pr_lock_cycles(trial, saved_cycles) for measurement-bound reference replay. Reports do not silently substitute historical results or enable reference overlays.

pr_inventory() retains every source path and flags identical content. pr_link_assets() requires explicit acquisition keys and rejects ambiguous joins. pr_read_workbook() preserves all sheets, row and column provenance, separate side-by-side HR series, and invalid observations. Numeric time units require an explicit choice. pr_read_asset() registers images; it never converts display colours to temperatures. Metadata inspection uses ExifTool when installed.

HTML reports require rmarkdown and Pandoc; PDF reports additionally require a working TeX installation. Workbook and archive importers require readxl and archive, respectively. The Shiny upload limit defaults to 128 MiB and can be set through options(pressR.max_upload_bytes = ...) before launching the app.

License

MIT

Citation

Use citation("pressR") for the installed version. Record the package version and source commit with each analysis. The previously advertised Zenodo identifier is a draft identifier that does not currently resolve; it is not presented as a published release DOI.

Use of LLM tools

Where applicable, LLM tools were used for narrowly defined, non-authorial tasks: copyediting, prose refinement, Markdown/LaTeX formatting, boilerplate scaffolding (such as CI configurations and build scripts), and code refactoring. Tools included Chat AI, the KISSKI (GWDG) service, and self-hosted Mistral Small (24B, Apache-2.0) served through a local vLLM architecture on an Ubuntu Linux workstation with Intel processors and NVIDIA GPUs. Self-hosted use also includes models that were further trained (fine-tuned) or weight-edited in-house for specific tasks. All self-hosted models ran locally, with no data sent to third parties.

All scientific claims, methodological choices, analyses, interpretations and conclusions remain the authors’ own. Where applicable, LLM-generated material must be reviewed and revised before inclusion, and references must be verified against their DOI, arXiv ID or ISBN.

Local software setup: vLLM with Python/PyTorch, plus R and RStudio.
